text:
praveen: Heads up — saw a large drop in prefix cache hit-rate after the kernel-selector bump (kernelex-v2). Affected /chat routes: hit-rate dropped ~72% -> ~39% for a subset of tool-heavy prompts. Posting the quick repro/logs we collected.

alex_chang: Can you paste the profiler/KV metrics? which part of the key looks different?

praveen: Quick profiler excerpt:

  KV cache: total_requests=12.4k, hits=4.8k, hits_pct=38.7%, prev_baseline_hits_pct=71.9%
  Top miss reasons (inferred): toolcall_serialization_variance, system_prompt_whitespace, tokenizer_version_mismatch

  Example serialized key (before change):
  {"prefix":"User: list files","tool_calls":[{"name":"ls","args":{"path":"/tmp"}}],"sys_prompt":"standard-v1"}

  Example (after change — introduced in kernelex-v2 canonicalizer):
  {"prefix":"User: list files","tool_calls":[{"name":"ls","args":{"path":"/tmp"}}],"sys_prompt":"standard-v1","tokenizer":"tknzr-3"}

  But the real problem is we now serialize tool_calls preserving caller-side ordering and whitespace in some args which means semantically identical prompts hash to different keys.

danielle: Confirmed — my change to include tool_calls metadata in the fingerprint didn't also canonicalize argument ordering or strip insignificant whitespace. Array order + JSON spacing differences will flip the hash.

maria_g: Also saw tokenizer changes cause subtle tokenization differences (extra newline -> different token split), so if tokenizer_version isn't pinned the same user request can map to a different normalized token sequence. That cascades into different cache keys.

praveen: From customer traces: many misses were for the same logical prompt but with tool args in different orders (some clients send args as map, some as ordered list).

alex_chang: Quick win: implement a deterministic key-normalizer that does the following:
  1) For tool_calls: convert args to sorted-key tuples, sort tool_calls by name then args hash.
  2) Trim trailing whitespace/newlines from system prompt and collapse internal multiple spaces to single spaces (config togglable).
  3) Include explicit tokenizer_version tag in key (e.g., "tknzr-3") so we can safely invalidate by version.
  4) Add key_schema_version field (key_schema_v=2) to allow gradual rollouts.

danielle: Proposed canonicalizer patch (pseudo):

  function canonicalize_key(payload) {
    payload.sys_prompt = normalize_spaces(payload.sys_prompt);
    payload.tool_calls = payload.tool_calls.map(tc => ({ name: tc.name, args: sortedObject(tc.args) }));
    payload.tool_calls.sort((a,b) => compareByNameArgs(a,b));
    return stableJSONStringify({ prefix: payload.prefix, tool_calls: payload.tool_calls, sys_prompt: payload.sys_prompt, tokenizer: payload.tokenizer, key_schema_v: "2" });
  }

maria_g: Also add logging for the first 100 keys per host with both old_hash and new_hash to audit collisions and misses (don't log PII).

warmup-bot: warmup-bot: scheduled "prefix-backfill" job at 09:00 UTC to warm up canonicalized keys for 10% of nodes (roster subset).

alex_chang: For immediate mitigation we can:
  - Roll a small canary of the key-normalizer v2 to 10% of hosts and measure hit-rate delta.
  - If success, expand to 50% and run a backfill warmup job during low traffic.
  - If customers still see regressions, enable per-route fallback that uses a relaxed fingerprint (strip tool_calls) for a short window.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary: key-normalizer v2 -> started on 10% at 08:40 UTC.

praveen: Canary results (first 30m): canary hit-rate ~68% (vs baseline 39%). P50 latency on canary nodes returned to expected bucket. Looks promising.

maria_g: After roll to 50% we should also run a tokenizer pin across service mesh to ensure no cross-node tokenizer mismatch. Plan: create a small metadata tag on request headers for tokenizer version and expose metric.

alex_chang: Added PR with code + tests + migration plan. PR link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/kernelex/pulls/812 (patch includes key_schema bump, canonicalizer, metrics).

praveen: Plan: roll to 50% tomorrow 02:00 UTC, run 2-hour warmup backfill, monitor hit-rate & cost. If stable, full rollout following day. Thanks all :thumbsup:

maria_g: Also note for postmortem: capture impact on billing (wasted tokens during miss spike) and include guidance for SDKs to send normalized tool args to reduce churn.

alex_chang: Agreed — adding a short SDK doc snippet and a compatibility note for tokenizer pinning.

praveen: Closing notes: root cause = inclusion of non-canonicalized tool_call serialization + whitespace/tokenizer drift. Fix = stable canonicalizer + tokenizer pin + key_schema versioning + warmup. Follow-ups assigned in the PR.
